title: Id like to share Rampallians with you - After 4 years of solo dev, my new card game is available to wishlist on steam! To get the art for the nearly 400 cards in this game done, we used traditional art as an input for Gen AI then touched up the output.
author: ElectricBrainUK
selftext:
Rampallians is a card game where you gather resources with gatherers, to play special, support, and unit cards. Building a settlement to fight your opponents in a 1v1.

There are 4 factions Orcs which are simple fast and aggressive. Humans which build out settlements to slowly improve their cards. Dwarves which are very adaptable and focus on making buildings and runes for the late game. Elves which harass and can do a lot of damage, but cant take too much! As well as some dragon cards that can be in any deck. Each card has their own unique traits and effects, with the best part of 400 cards in total. All available in the full game, no packs, no extra purchases of any kind.

Rampallians is a game that I solo developed over 4 years, but that doesn't do it justice because I had a lot of help from very lovely people. Myself and 3 of my friends came up with the idea and spent a lot of time iterating on it until we got to this stage.

Part of what we wanted to achieve was to make a card game that wasn't pay to win. Which is possibly why we went to such lengths with the number of diverse cards and effects. Any future content will be included for free, no packs or dlc. I'd also like to explore the possibility of user generated content if we were lucky enough to have an audience that was interested. All of the cards and effects are JSON files so can be easily edited (both players have to agree on a set of cards to prevent cheating).

My brother made the music for the game which I think is really nice and fitting, it flows based on what you're doing in the game, be it at the main menu, in game, or in combat. With transitions to go between them.

Finally how I used AI. Something I have been heavily critisied for is the use of ai in the artwork. My mum and a family friend were kind enough to help me do the art for the cards. But it was taking too long given as I mentioned there are 400 cards, and sadly we don't have the funds to pay a professional. So we came up with a process where the artists sketched the cards, then filled in detail with an SDXL plugin for Krita, before then correcting the output manually. I wonder how people here feel about this hybrid approach, I've made a video explaining in more detail here if people are interested:

[https://youtu.be/FPFsaAz0yDo?si=txSjAHtztnOszSnJ](https://youtu.be/FPFsaAz0yDo?si=txSjAHtztnOszSnJ)

Thanks for reading if you've got down to here, if you'd like to check the steam page here is the link:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4363230/Rampallians/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4363230/Rampallians/)

I'd love to hear your thoughts, and really appreciate any feedback! Also happy to share more details on the process.

P.s. I'll have a demo in the upcoming next fest. The aim is to have the demo act as a trial of the full game, with two decks (no deck builder like in the full game), but you'll be able to play with players who have the full game when that comes out later in the year.

comments.author: angrylittledev
comments.body: What did you use for visual effects like swirling of that portal gate, and other visual effects?

replies.author: ElectricBrainUK
replies.body: A mixture - the swirling portal effect is an ai generated image through the same process as the card art, then unity particle system on top, as well as a bloom effect. The visual effects are all just particle system effects in unity, I used this asset as a base: [https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/vfx/board-card-game-stylized-vfx-magic-213764](https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/vfx/board-card-game-stylized-vfx-magic-213764)

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: I see, thanks. I was hoping there was an AI local run tool that I could use to make effects for my own games and art.

replies.author: ElectricBrainUK
replies.body: You can definitly create particles in sdxl, you will then have to manually cut around them for the transparency stuff. Or I have had some luck with this background remover in comfyui but it often leaves a bit of a border: [https://github.com/1038lab/ComfyUI-RMBG](https://github.com/1038lab/ComfyUI-RMBG)

comments.author: Ali_ibs
comments.body: This looks amazing. AI is the way for single devs to make complex and beautiful games like this. Vocal minority will complain, but most people will enjoy a great game. Did you do the coding yourself, or also some  AI?

replies.author: ElectricBrainUK
replies.body: Predominately coded myself, I did use gemini assist and github co pilot for code completion and to generate some little bits and pieces. Mostly just because it wasnt really there when I first started

replies.author: ElectricBrainUK
replies.body: Sorry long day, I just went straight into answer the question mode. I also wanted to say thanks very much for the kind comment, I really appreciate it and you taking the time to check out the game!

comments.author: TurnYourBrightsOFF
comments.body: Added to my Wishlist.  Can't wait to play it.  I like how you're open to sharing the development details.   Initial impressions is that it looks fun, a little overwhelming at the same time.  I'd hope there is a good tutorial and mouse hover tooltips for all the icons/slots that I have no idea what they are.

replies.author: ElectricBrainUK
replies.body:
Ah thanks very much I really appreciate it! There is a lot to it, but you're right, tooltips for all of the keywords and icons, as well as two tutorials one covering the basics and another combat. 

Thanks again for checking it out!
